feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Adding a signature that covers the witness weight addresses significant concerns related to witness malleability in Bitcoin transactions. This approach does not entirely prevent all forms of witness malleability, particularly those that can create complications for mechanisms such as compact blocks. However, it effectively mitigates the most problematic aspect for users: the manipulation by malicious relay nodes who could otherwise artificially inflate the witness data. Such inflation reduces the transaction’s fee-rate, potentially disadvantaging the user.
While constructing Bitcoin Scripts to inherently avoid witness malleability is advisable, achieving this goal remains challenging. As scripts become more intricate, ensuring immutability becomes increasingly complex and in some cases may not be feasible at all. The introduction of Schnorr signatures, as detailed in the relevant BIP, introduces a fixed-size signature. This development simplifies the calculation of the witness weight prior to signing, offering a practical improvement for script designers and users alike.
In scenarios involving complex multi-party signing protocols, not all participants may be aware of the final witness weight at the moment of signing. To accommodate these situations, the feature allowing the signature to cover witness weight should remain optional rather than mandatory. This flexibility enables broader compatibility and adaptability across diverse transaction types and signing arrangements.
